name: Build, Ship, Shape: Amazon Developer Hackathon
theme: Build or significantly update working applications across Fire TV, Alexa+, Bee, or Ring, and provide developer-product feedback.
tracks: AWS Builder — optional mini challenge alongside a primary track
Open Source — optional mini challenge alongside a primary track
build_window: Official submission and qualifying development period: 2026-08-31 10:15 America/Los_Angeles through 2026-10-23 12:00 America/Los_Angeles. Existing projects must be significantly updated during this period.
team_size: 1 developer plus AI coding tools; no other teammates confirmed
required_tech: Conditional on Fire TV entry: run on Fire OS or Vega OS; any framework or language is acceptable.

Conditional on Alexa+ entry: working Agent Skill, self-hosted MCP server using specification 2025-11-25 or later over Streamable HTTP, or a working simulated Alexa+ experience using any AI or agentic tool. The simulation alternative has no mandatory framework, SDK, or MCP interface.
Conditional on Bee entry: Bee CLI, MCP, or Agent Skills connected to actual data recorded and processed through a Bee device or Apple Watch running Bee software.
Conditional on Ring entry: a Ring API, SDK, simulator, or device listed in Ring developer documentation.

Conditional on AWS Builder entry: documented qualifying AWS integration or documented use of Kiro Crew during development; a separate AWS runtime service is unnecessary when qualifying through Kiro Crew.
encouraged_tech: Amazon Devices Builder Tools MCP server and Agent Skills for development assistance.
Fire TV starter samples; React Native, web technologies, and Android Kotlin/Java are suggested implementation options.
AWS services and tools such as Bedrock, AgentCore, Strands SDK, Kiro Crew, and SageMaker are optional outside AWS Builder.
Cross-device integrations are permitted but are not mandatory.
required_or_encouraged_tech: Track-dependent platforms: Fire OS, Vega OS, Alexa+ simulation, Agent Skills, MCP, Bee developer tools, and Ring developer interfaces.
Optional development support: Amazon Devices Builder Tools, public starter repositories, documentation, and community resources.
Optional AWS Builder technologies: qualifying AWS services or Kiro Crew.

requirements.description: Mandatory: register through the event's Devpost site and complete all required submission fields before the deadline.

Mandatory: individual participants must meet their jurisdiction's age of majority. Geographic, promotion-entity, judge, affiliate, family/household, and conflict-of-interest exclusions apply. Named excluded locations include Brazil, Quebec, Russia, Crimea, Cuba, Iran, and North Korea; the list is not exhaustive.
Conditional mandatory: teams and organizations must authorize an eligible representative to submit on their behalf. No official maximum team size.

Mandatory: enter a qualifying primary track and identify the selected primary track(s) and any mini challenges in the submission. Each project can win at most one track prize and one mini-challenge prize.
Mandatory: provide a working application newly created or significantly updated during the submission period. For an existing project, explain and demonstrate the qualifying changes.
Conditional mandatory for Fire TV: run on Fire OS or Vega OS and show functioning software on an actual Fire TV device or accepted emulator/simulator. Framework choice is unrestricted.

Conditional mandatory for Alexa+: demonstrate a working Agent Skill, a self-hosted MCP server using specification 2025-11-25 or later over Streamable HTTP, or a working simulated Alexa+ experience. The simulation alternative requires source code and a functioning demonstration but no specific SDK, framework, or MCP-shaped interface.

Conditional mandatory for Bee: use actual data recorded and processed through a Bee device or Apple Watch running Bee software via Bee CLI, MCP, or Agent Skills. Code and video must demonstrate actual Bee-data interaction delivering user value. Public onboarding of other Bee users is unnecessary.
Conditional mandatory for Ring: use a documented Ring API, SDK, simulator, or device and demonstrate the application through an accepted simulator or actual device. Physical hardware is optional.

Conditional mandatory for Alexa+ nonsimulation, Bee, and Ring: repository code must actually use the qualifying technology through runtime calls, entry points, or loaded agent/flow/MCP configuration. README mentions alone do not qualify. Alexa+ simulations and Fire TV have their separately specified alternatives.
Mandatory: submit a text description explaining project features, functionality, and operation.

Mandatory: provide a GitHub repository containing all necessary source code, assets, and clear setup/run instructions. Use either a public repository with a detectable open-source license or a private repository shared with the specified Amazon and Devpost reviewers.

Conditional mandatory for private repositories: share with Amazon reviewers knmeiss, giolaq, anishamalde, mosesroth, emersonsklar and the specified Devpost reviewer before the deadline. The supplied evidence redacts the Devpost email address; resolve it from the official source. Invitations require acceptance and expire after seven days.

Mandatory: provide a public YouTube or Vimeo demonstration video and its submission-form link, showing the project functioning on the intended accepted platform. Target less than three minutes; judges need not watch beyond three minutes. Third-party media and trademarks require appropriate rights.
Mandatory: for every tool, API, or SDK used, explain its purpose, strengths, shortcomings, onboarding experience, and whether and why the entrant would use it again.

Mandatory: make the project available free of charge and without testing restrictions to sponsor, administrator, and judges through the judging period ending November 20, 2026 at 12:00 Pacific Time. Provide credentials for private websites when applicable. The FAQ permits a locally runnable repository and video without continuous hosting.
Mandatory: provide submission materials in English or supply English translations, including the video, description, documentation, and testing instructions.

Mandatory: satisfy originality, ownership, privacy, and intellectual-property requirements; obtain authorization for third-party APIs, SDKs, data, and media, and comply with open-source licenses. Sponsor/administrator financial or preferential support restrictions also apply.
Conditional mandatory when entering multiple submissions: each must be unique and substantially different from the entrant's other submissions.

Conditional mandatory if entering AWS Builder: document qualifying AWS use and describe the services and their use in product feedback. Kiro Crew development use alone qualifies without a separate AWS runtime service.

Conditional mandatory if entering Open Source: provide a new additional licensed open-source project or public-repository contribution made during the hackathon window alongside the primary-track submission. Include contribution URL, project repository URL, GitHub username, and what changed, how it works, and why it matters. An unmerged branch, fork, or PR is acceptable.
Optional: submit friction logs covering task, steps, expected versus actual result, severity, workaround, and actionable suggestion. These can receive up to a 10% judging bonus.
Optional: include feature requests explaining the request, its importance, and priority as critical, important, or nice-to-have.

submission_artifacts: Completed Devpost submission with primary-track and optional mini-challenge selections.
Text description of features and functionality.
GitHub repository with source code, assets, and setup/run instructions; public with open-source license or private with authorized reviewer access.
Public YouTube or Vimeo demo-video URL.
Product feedback for every tool, API, or SDK used.
For pre-existing projects: explanation and demonstration of significant changes during the submission period.
When applicable: testing credentials and English translations.
For AWS Builder: qualifying-use documentation and AWS-use explanation in product feedback.
For Open Source: contribution URL, project repository URL, GitHub username, and contribution explanation.
Optional friction logs and feature requests.
demo_requirements: Show the project actually functioning on its intended accepted platform.
Video should be less than three minutes; judges are not required to watch beyond three minutes.
Publish on YouTube or Vimeo with public visibility and include its URL in the submission.
Provide English narration/materials or English translation under the formal rules.
Fire TV: show actual Fire TV hardware or an accepted emulator/simulator.
Alexa+: show the selected Agent Skill, MCP server, or simulated experience functioning. A real web MCP client is accepted; real Alexa+ device integration is unnecessary.
Bee: demonstrate actual Bee-data interaction producing user value in both code and video.
Ring: demonstrate through a documented simulator or actual Ring device.
Existing projects: demonstrate the significant new functionality.
Use third-party media or trademarks only with appropriate rights.
data_requirements: Bee track only: actual data recorded and processed through a Bee device or Apple Watch running Bee software is mandatory; synthetic-only substitutes do not establish compliance.
Any third-party data used must be authorized under applicable terms and licensing requirements.
No shared competition dataset or mandatory dataset size is identified.
prizes: Total advertised cash: $138,000; advertised combined cash and AWS-credit value: $190,000.
Fire TV: first $25,000 cash plus $15,000 AWS credits; second $15,000 cash plus $5,000 credits; third $4,000 cash plus $1,000 credits.
Alexa+: first $25,000 cash plus $15,000 AWS credits; second $15,000 cash plus $5,000 credits; third $4,000 cash plus $1,000 credits.
AWS Builder: one $5,000 cash prize plus $5,000 AWS credits.
Open Source: one $5,000 cash prize plus $5,000 AWS credits.
Listed winners receive Amazon Developer channel features; primary-track first-place and mini-challenge winners also receive an Amazon Developer team meeting.
Each project may win at most one track prize and one mini-challenge prize; awards remain subject to eligibility and winner verification.

facts.claim: The official submission period runs August 31, 2026 at 10:15 Pacific Time through October 23, 2026 at 12:00 Pacific Time.
The deadline corresponds to October 23, 2026 at 19:00 UTC and 20:00 Europe/London.
facts.source: src-41e7f619fb22; supplied official rules and updates

facts.claim: Stage One is a pass/fail assessment of baseline viability, theme fit, and appropriate required-technology use. Stage Two uses four equally weighted criteria.
Friction logs are optional. Internal Stage One reviewers recommend a bonus up to 10%, which the Stage Two panel applies to the final spreadsheet score.
Ties are resolved by comparing criteria in listed order, beginning with Tech Implementation, then Design, Potential Impact, and Quality of the Idea; remaining ties go to a panel vote.
Judging is scheduled November 9–20, 2026, with winners announced on or around December 3, 2026.
There is no maximum team size; solo entrants and organizations may enter.
Gated Alexa+ Category SDK, MCP Toolkit, CLI, and Web Simulator access is unavailable to hackathon participants. The FAQ permits self-hosted integrations and entrant-built simulation/front-end paths.
A locally runnable repository and demo video can satisfy Alexa+ judging access; an MCP server need not remain continuously live after submission.
The October 7 update states that AWS promotional credit codes are exhausted and requests are no longer accepted.
Official rules take precedence over conflicting website, form, or promotional statements.

The operator supplies a one-developer constraint, approximately 10 focused build hours, and unconfirmed hardware/AWS runtime access. These are participant circumstances rather than official event rules.
facts.source: Operator constraints supplied directly in the task

judging_criteria.name: Stage One qualification
judging_criteria.notes: Baseline viability, reasonable theme fit, and appropriate use of qualifying APIs/SDKs, subject to the explicit track alternatives.

judging_criteria.name: Tech Implementation
judging_criteria.weight_or_priority: 25% of base Stage Two score; first tie-break criterion
judging_criteria.notes: Build quality and effective use of the selected track or mini-challenge technology and device capabilities.

judging_criteria.name: Design
judging_criteria.weight_or_priority: 25% of base Stage Two score; second tie-break criterion
judging_criteria.notes: Complete, coherent product experience and intuitive interaction appropriate to the device or platform.

judging_criteria.name: Potential Impact
judging_criteria.weight_or_priority: 25% of base Stage Two score; third tie-break criterion
judging_criteria.notes: Credible, specific customer need and realistic value to an audience beyond the hackathon.

judging_criteria.name: Quality of the Idea
judging_criteria.weight_or_priority: 25% of base Stage Two score; fourth tie-break criterion
judging_criteria.notes: Creative use of tools and demonstrated understanding of the ecosystem and end-user needs. Rules explicitly distinguish obvious implementations from more substantive work.

judging_criteria.name: Optional friction-log bonus
judging_criteria.notes: Internal Stage One review recommends a bonus to the Stage Two panel. Exact arithmetic is unspecified; the bonus should not be interpreted as a fifth equally weighted criterion.

sanitized_brief: Build, Ship, Shape: Amazon Developer Hackathon. Submission deadline: 2026-10-23 12:00 PDT, 19:00 UTC, 20:00 Europe/London. Official qualifying period: August 31, 2026 at 10:15 Pacific Time through the deadline; existing projects require significant changes during that period. Primary tracks are Fire TV, Alexa+, Bee, and Ring. Fire TV requires functioning Fire OS or Vega OS software demonstrated on accepted hardware or an emulator/simulator; framework choice is unrestricted. Alexa+ accepts an Agent Skill, self-hosted MCP specification 2025-11-25+ over Streamable HTTP, or a working simulated Alexa+ experience with no mandated framework or MCP interface. Gated Alexa+ partner tooling is unavailable to participants. Bee requires actual Bee-origin data from a Bee device or Apple Watch running Bee software, accessed through Bee CLI, MCP, or Agent Skills and demonstrated delivering user value. Ring accepts documented APIs, SDKs, simulators, or devices and requires an actual-device or simulator demonstration. AWS Builder and Open Source are optional mini challenges with additional documentation requirements; Kiro Crew development use alone can qualify for AWS Builder. Required artifacts include a project description, GitHub repository with complete source/assets/setup instructions, public YouTube or Vimeo functioning-demo video targeted below three minutes, tool-by-tool product feedback, and track selections. Public repositories require an open-source license; private repositories require specified reviewer access. Materials must be English or accompanied by English translations. A locally runnable Alexa+ repository plus video is acceptable without continuous deployment. Stage One is a viability/theme/technology pass-fail gate. Stage Two evaluates Tech Implementation, Design, Potential Impact, and Quality of the Idea equally at 25% each; ties follow that order. Optional friction logs can earn up to a 10% bonus. Priority areas include Fire TV viewing, sports, fitness, family entertainment, multimodal UX and computer vision; Bee education, developer experience and productivity; and Ring access control, business systems, automation, accessibility and caretaking. These priorities are optional. Useful capabilities include public device starter code, simulators, documentation, Amazon Devices Builder Tools, and optional AWS services. Promotional AWS credit requests are closed. No common dataset is supplied. Crowding labels reflect organizer descriptions of obvious work, not measured entry frequency: basic media players, single-turn chatbots/API wrappers, wearable logging/notification relays, basic motion alerts/live views, superficial AWS use, and trivial open-source edits have high differentiation risk. No evidence establishes medium-collision or underexplored categories. Participant constraints supplied by the operator are one developer plus AI tools, approximately 10 focused build hours, and unconfirmed hardware and AWS runtime access; these are not official rules. Live account status and live rule amendments remain unverified.
